userStories.title: createLocalIssueOnMain primitive (commit-tree to main)
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need a dependency-injected primitive that appends a local issue to scripts/cam/issues.local.json on main (read-from-main id allocation, off-main commit-tree, on-main direct commit) so filing from a feature branch never entangles the backlog or races next_id.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/commands/issue-file.ts exports createLocalIssueOnMain(options), mirroring the SpawnFn/ClockFn injectable types and DI'd-reader style of src/commands/ship-finalize.ts. [oracle: grep -q 'export function createLocalIssueOnMain' src/commands/issue-file.ts]

The current backlog is read from main via 'git show main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json' through the injected spawnFn and JSON.parsed (NOT from the working tree), so id allocation is collision-free. [oracle: grep -q 'main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json' src/commands/issue-file.ts]

The new entry id is the issue_prefix (read from project.toml, default CAM) joined to next_id; next_id is bumped and the appended entry has state 'open', createdAt from clock(), and an optional priority field. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]
The updated backlog is serialized with JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) plus a trailing newline. [oracle: grep -q 'null, 2' src/commands/issue-file.ts]

The current branch is determined via 'git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD'; when it equals 'main' the function writes the working-tree file, git adds it, and git commits; otherwise it takes the off-main commit-tree path and leaves the working tree and feature-branch HEAD untouched. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

The off-main path uses git plumbing: a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree main, hash-object -w --stdin (fed the updated JSON), update-index --add --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree -p main, and update-ref refs/heads/main. [oracle: grep -q 'commit-tree' src/commands/issue-file.ts]
createLocalIssueOnMain returns { id, committedTo: 'main', sha, branchWasMain }. [oracle: grep -q 'committedTo' src/commands/issue-file.ts]
The commit message is the literal form 'chore(cam): file <id> (<title>)'. [oracle: grep -q 'chore(cam): file ' src/commands/issue-file.ts]

test/issue-file.test.ts uses recording-spawn fakes (mirroring test/ship-finalize.test.ts) and asserts the git argv sequence for BOTH the on-main path and the off-main commit-tree path. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

The off-main unit test asserts the injected spawnFn receives the temp GIT_INDEX_FILE via its options env AND the updated-JSON via its options input/stdin (for 'git hash-object -w --stdin'), pinning the widened SpawnFn type so hash-object's stdin cannot be routed around the injection. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Mirror src/commands/ship-finalize.ts: same exported ClockFn type, same injectable-reader style, same exported result interface. MANDATORY widened SpawnFn: the exported SpawnFn type for this primitive MUST accept an optional env (Record<string,string>) and an optional input (string) in its options arg, i.e. a strict superset of ship-finalize's { encoding: 'utf8' }. AC#1's 'mirroring the SpawnFn/ClockFn injectable types' means mirror the STYLE, extending the options to carry env + input. The off-main path requires this: GIT_INDEX_FILE goes through options.env (pointing at a mktemp index) and the updated JSON is fed to 'git hash-object -w --stdin' through options.input/stdin. Keep all git calls injectable so the unit test never shells out. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex access (patterns.md). Read issue_prefix via parseToml(readProjectToml()) like finalizeCycleClose. Files: src/commands/issue-file.ts, test/issue-file.test.ts. Read patterns.md 'finalizeCycleClose hardening pattern' and 'issues.local.json hygiene (CAM-47)' before coding.

userStories.title: Real-git integration test for file-on-main
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need a real-git integration test proving the commit-tree-to-main path actually lands the entry on main while leaving the feature branch and working tree untouched, because unit fakes record argv and return success regardless of what real git would do.
acceptanceCriteria: New integration test test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts mkdtempSyncs a fresh repo, runs git init, configures user.email and user.name, seeds scripts/cam/issues.local.json on main with a known next_id, and commits it. [oracle: grep -q 'mkdtempSync' test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts]

Case A (off-main): after checking out a feature branch and running createLocalIssueOnMain with a realSpawnFn over spawnSync, the new entry exists on main (git show main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json), the feature-branch HEAD is unchanged, and the working tree is clean (git status --porcelain is empty). [oracle: bun test test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts]

Case B (on-main): running createLocalIssueOnMain while checked out on main lands a direct commit on main and the working-tree file contains the new entry. [oracle: bun test test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts]

The test skips cleanly when git is absent (test.skipIf over spawnSync git --version), mirroring test/integration/ship-finalize-dirty-prd.test.ts, and registers temp dirs in an afterEach rmSync cleanup. [oracle: grep -q 'skipIf' test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Mirror test/integration/ship-finalize-dirty-prd.test.ts and patterns.md 'Real-git integration test pattern (US-004, CAM-72)': mkdtempSync in tmpdir, git init, git config user.email/user.name (required for commit), seed+stage+commit baseline on main, run with realSpawnFn wrapping spawnSync, assert with real git show / git status --porcelain / git rev-parse. The realSpawnFn wrapper MUST forward the optional env (GIT_INDEX_FILE) and input/stdin (for hash-object --stdin) introduced in US-001, or the off-main path will not exercise correctly. The tmpdir has NO remote, so do not assume origin exists (US-005 guard must already tolerate that). Files: test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts.

userStories.description: As an orchestrator, I need a deterministic 'cam issue --file-local' that reads { title, description, priority? } as JSON from stdin and routes to createLocalIssueOnMain before the runIssue thin-proxy, mirroring 'cam ship --finalize', so the free-text proxy path is never invoked for deterministic filing.
acceptanceCriteria: parseIssueArgs recognizes --file-local and returns a discriminated shape (e.g. { mode: 'file-local' }) distinct from the existing free-text { text } shape. [oracle: grep -q 'file-local' index.ts]

A new exported dispatchIssue(parsed, deps?) routes the file-local mode to createLocalIssueOnMain BEFORE the runIssue thin-proxy, mirroring how dispatchShip branches to finalizeCycleClose before runShip. [oracle: grep -q 'export async function dispatchIssue' index.ts]

The --file-local path reads { title, description, priority? } as JSON from STDIN (no argv escaping of arbitrary text), built by a new _buildCreateIssueOpts(cwd, parsedStdin) that wires production deps (spawnSync, ISO clock, stdin read). [oracle: grep -q '_buildCreateIssueOpts' index.ts]
A dispatch unit test injects fakes for both branches and proves --file-local NEVER calls the runIssue thin-proxy. [oracle: bun test]
The case 'issue' block in main() routes through dispatchIssue rather than calling runIssue directly. [oracle: grep -q 'dispatchIssue' index.ts]
No --permission-mode CLI flag is registered (enforced by test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts). [oracle: bun test test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Mirror the ship dispatch in index.ts: parseShipArgs (index.ts:706), dispatchShip + ShipDispatchDeps (index.ts:740), _buildFinalizeOpts (index.ts:759), and the case 'ship' wiring (index.ts:914). The existing free-text runIssue (src/commands/issue.ts) single-hub thin-proxy stays as the no-flag path; --file-local is the deterministic in-process surface like ship --finalize. parseIssueArgs is at index.ts:466 and case 'issue' at index.ts:874. userStories.title: Up-to-date-main guard + push on file-on-main
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need createLocalIssueOnMain to refuse to commit a divergent local main and to push origin/main after committing, so a stale local main does not silently fork the backlog and a filed issue actually reaches the remote.
acceptanceCriteria: Before mutating, createLocalIssueOnMain (or a thin wrapper) checks local main against origin/main (git rev-parse main vs git rev-parse origin/main, after a best-effort git fetch); on divergence it does NOT commit, surfaces a printError, and returns a structured outcome the caller can act on. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

When origin/main is absent (no remote configured), the up-to-date check is skipped rather than treated as divergence, so the real-git tmpdir test (US-002, no remote) still passes. [oracle: bun test test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts]

After committing, 'git push origin main' runs best-effort with explicit success/failure logging; a push rejection is reported, never swallowed. [oracle: grep -q "'push', 'origin', 'main'" src/commands/issue-file.ts]
Detached HEAD and a missing local main branch are handled with clear errors. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]
All new git calls go through the injected spawnFn; the unit test asserts the guard short-circuits on divergence and the push argv fires on the success path. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Layer the guard into src/commands/issue-file.ts. Use printError from src/logging/color.ts (precedent: finalizeCycleClose hard-failure path). CRITICAL compat: the US-002 integration tmpdir has no remote, so a missing origin/main must SKIP the up-to-date check (not abort) and push must be best-effort (missing remote => log, do not fail). Keep git fetch / rev-parse / push all on the injected spawnFn so the unit test asserts argv with no network. Files: src/commands/issue-file.ts, test/issue-file.test.ts.
